name: Enenlhet
confidence_why: Wheeler 2023, the only study to examine Enenlhet stress, found no word-position effect on vowel duration and so no evidence for fixed stress, leaving open whether the language lacks word stress or has lexically specified stress, and the sole descriptive grammar guide, Unruh, Kalisch & Romero 2003, says nothing about word stress, so no placement or type can be asserted.

catalog_quote: 5.2. Stress -- There is no independent word position effect in the corpus, and therefore no evidence for fixed stress. Future research is needed to determine if Enenlhet lacks word-level stress entirely. Alternatively, stress may be lexically specified, variable based on word class, or some morphemes may fall outside the stress domain and therefore obscure stress in this analysis. [p. 3425] ... If Enenlhet has fixed stress, it was expected to be identifiable as a lengthening effect associated with a vowel’s position within a word. new_statements.rule_in_words: Corpus-phonetic study (3.5 h naturalistic speech, 8 speakers, 15,031 vowels, linear mixed-effects model): vowel duration shows no effect of position within the word (counted from either edge), so there is no durational evidence for fixed positional word stress. The author leaves open whether Enenlhet has no word-level stress at all, or lexically specified / word-class-dependent stress that duration cannot detect. No source gives a positive stress-placement rule; the only pedagogical grammar (Unruh, Kalisch & Romero 2003, pp. 300-301) describes the orthography and geminate consonants but never states where stress falls.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the author notes stress might be lexical, vary by word class, or be obscured by morphemes outside the stress domain. Enenlhet is stated (Unruh & Kalisch 2003; Wheeler 2023 p. 3422) to lack contrastive vowel length, unlike Enlhet Norte and Enxet Sur; consonant gemination is contrastive (Unruh et al. 2003 p. 90). Utterance-final lengthening is restricted to the last vowel of the utterance-final word (p. 3424).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level, measured in connected naturalistic speech (interviews/narratives), enclitics counted with the host word; the only positive 'acento' remark in Unruh et al. 2003 (p. 110) is phrase-level focus emphasis on the preverbal word, and 'entonación' (p. 83) is described as phrase melody.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources concern Enenlhet = Toba-Enenlhet = Toba-Maskoy [tmf] = toba1268, the Enlhet-Enenlhet language of Casanillo / Pozo Amarillo (Unruh, Kalisch & Romero 2003 is based on the Toba of the Complejo Casanillo; Wheeler 2023 uses the Heaton 2019 AILLA corpus, 8 speakers). Not to be confused with Toba-Qom [tob] (Guaycuruan), which is what Susnik's 'Emok-Toba' and Schmidt 1962 refer to (Fabre 2005 sec. 8, fn. 47, 49). Enlhet [enl] is the sister language Enlhet Norte (nort2971).

sources.note: Sec. 5.2 (p. 3425): no word-position effect on vowel duration, 'therefore no evidence for fixed stress'; unresolved whether Enenlhet lacks word stress entirely or has lexical/word-class stress. Three vowels /a e o/, no contrastive vowel length; utterance-final, open-syllable and pre-voiced-consonant lengthening found.
